title: RFID Loyalty Cards — NFC Reward Cards for Retail
summary: RFID loyalty cards are contactless NFC reward cards customers tap at the POS; the tap takes under 1 second and needs no app download. Points post without cashier intervention — the reader captures the UID in under 100 ms and passes it to the loyalty engine. Chips span NTAG213 to MIFARE DESFire EV3; custom-printed cards start at MOQ 500 with 10-12 business day production.
heroPoints: Tap-to-earn at POS. Customer taps their NFC loyalty card on the terminal; the transaction is recorded and points are updated instantly with no barcode scanning or manual entry.
Premium brand experience: custom-printed PVC cards with full-color artwork, spot UV, metallic foil and embossing create a card customers keep in their wallet instead of discarding.
No app required: unlike mobile loyalty programs that require customers to download, register and maintain an app, NFC loyalty cards work out of the box with zero setup friction.

brief.label: Card body and form factor
items: ISO/IEC 7810 ID-1 (85.60 × 53.98 × 0.76 mm) PVC is the retail-wallet default; fits every existing loyalty-card rack, slot and wallet divider.
Die-cut keytag (30 × 55 mm) and half-card (ISO 7810 ID-2 shortened) options for keyring attachment or wallet-depth constraints.

brief.label: Loyalty-programme market context
items: Global loyalty-programme membership tracked by Bond Brand Loyalty and Forrester; U.S. adults belong to ~16 loyalty programmes on average but are active in only ~7.
Active-use rate and visit-lift are the metrics programme owners report against, not enrolment — a card that stays in the wallet is the structural win.

brief.label: Chip selection aligned to loyalty data model
items: NTAG213 (144 B) — URL / UID-based member lookup for SMB and mid-market; the cheapest credible NFC loyalty card.
NTAG216 (888 B) — NDEF multi-record payload where a welcome promo + member-ID URL is useful on first tap.
MIFARE Classic 1K — 16-sector memory for multi-merchant mall / plaza loyalty programmes where sector-per-merchant separation is valued.
MIFARE DESFire EV3 — AES-128 per-card key diversification where member-credit or prepaid balance is stacked onto the loyalty card.

brief.label: Tap-to-earn POS flow
items: Customer taps loyalty card on NFC reader at the POS; UID read in < 100 ms and passed to the loyalty engine (Yotpo, Annex Cloud, Smile.io, Voucherify, Loyalty Lion, custom).
Loyalty engine resolves UID → member record → applies points, tier, basket-promo, birthday reward; POS prints receipt within the normal transaction envelope.

brief.label: Digital overlay — tap on phone
items: NDEF URI record `https://brand.example.com/loyalty?m={uid}` opens the member dashboard on a stock iPhone (iOS 12+ Background Tag Reading) or Android phone — no app install.
Apple Wallet Passes and Google Wallet loyalty cards can mirror the physical card with barcode + latest balance; physical card keeps the wallet-slot presence.

brief.label: Dual-interface — NFC + barcode
items: Printed 1D (Code 128) or 2D (QR) barcode on the card as a fallback for POS lanes still waiting on NFC hardware; the same member-ID is encoded both ways.
Barcode print-quality target: ISO/IEC 15416 grade A/B so handheld / in-counter scanners read reliably on first pass.

brief.label: Anti-fraud posture
items: Unique chip UID (NTAG 7-byte / MIFARE 4-byte) replaces trivially-clonable punch cards and printed barcodes; UID replay is detectable server-side.
NTAG213 32-bit password protection or DESFire EV3 AES-128 raises the bar to cryptographic attack for premium / high-reward programmes.

brief.label: Data-protection posture — GDPR and equivalents
items: GDPR (EU) 2016/679 Art. 6 lawful-basis analysis: loyalty runs on consent (Art. 6(1)(a)) or contract (Art. 6(1)(b)) depending on how the programme terms are written.
Member right-of-access (Art. 15), erasure (Art. 17) and portability (Art. 20) must be supported in the loyalty-engine back-end; card is purely a UID carrier.

brief.label: PCI-DSS scope where payment is stacked
items: If the loyalty card also carries a stored-value balance or is linked to a payment credential, PCI-DSS v4.0 scope applies to the back-end and POS integration path — not to the card itself.
Pure loyalty-only UID cards are out of PCI-DSS scope; the card becomes in-scope only when payment data is linked.

brief.label: Premium finishing and wallet retention
items: Spot UV, metallic foil (gold / silver / holographic), soft-touch lamination and embossed card numbers earn wallet-slot residency versus the trivially-replaced paper punch card.
Transparent and frosted-PVC options are gaining share in premium-retail / beauty / fashion programmes for a differentiated shelf-appeal versus commodity PVC.

brief.label: Programme lifecycle — issuance, tiering, suspension
items: Issuance: POS-activated at first purchase; POS issues physical card + seeds member record. Tiering: back-end rule engine updates tier; card UID stays the same.
Suspension / replacement: back-end flags UID as revoked; customer gets a new card with new UID mapped to the same member record.

brief.label: Production flow and lead time
items: Artwork → proof → offset print (MOQ 500) or UV digital (MOQ 100) with variable-data QR → lamination → punch → NTAG / MIFARE encoding (UID registration + optional NDEF URL).
Standard lead time 10–12 business days; rush 7-day turnaround available for promotional launches; free samples after artwork lock.

sections.title: Why retailers choose NFC loyalty cards over app-only programs
bullets: App fatigue — 75% of downloaded loyalty apps are used once and then deleted or ignored; customers resist downloading yet another app for each store they visit. NFC cards require zero digital onboarding and work for all demographics including customers without smartphones.

Checkout speed: barcode-based loyalty cards require the cashier to scan (adding 5-10 seconds per transaction) or the customer to open an app and navigate to their digital card (adding 15-30 seconds); NFC tap takes under 1 second.
Wallet presence: a well-designed physical card in the customer's wallet is a constant brand reminder; app icons buried on the third screen of a phone have near-zero brand visibility.

Fraud reduction: paper punch cards and generic barcoded cards are trivially duplicated; NFC cards with unique chip IDs and optional NTAG213 password protection prevent customers from cloning their loyalty credential to accumulate fraudulent points.

In-store analytics: every tap is recorded with timestamp, terminal ID and transaction amount; retailers gain precise visit frequency and spending pattern data without depending on customers remembering to use an app.

sections.title: Active-use gap — why the card matters more than the enrolment

dataHighlight.heading: Average U.S. consumer is enrolled in ~16 loyalty programmes but active in only ~7
dataHighlight.text: Bond Brand Loyalty and Forrester research consistently shows U.S. adults enrol in roughly 16 loyalty programmes and actively use about 7. The gap is dominated by wallet-slot presence and redemption friction. A well-designed NFC loyalty card that is physically in the customer's wallet, taps cleanly at the POS and opens a member-dashboard page on phone-tap is significantly more likely to stay in the active-7 than a paper card or an app that demands onboarding and attention. This is the structural reason retailers keep investing in premium physical cards even while building wallet and app layers alongside them — the card carries the programme through the moments the phone or app cannot.

sections.title: Anatomy of the card — coil, chip, and a wallet-worthy shell
sections.intro: Electrically a loyalty card is almost nothing: a printed PVC sandwich, a copper antenna coil, and one NFC chip. The engineering that actually reaches the customer is the finishing — the spot UV, foil and soft-touch that decide whether the card earns a wallet slot or a spot in the bin. Push the artwork through [custom card printing](/products/rfid-cards/nfc-card-custom-printing/) once the chip is locked.

image.alt: Cutaway of an RFID loyalty card. Left, the lamination stack: printed front overlay with artwork and spot UV, a PVC core carrying the antenna coil and NFC chip module, and a printed back overlay with the fallback barcode and card number; 85.60 × 53.98 × 0.76 mm, ISO/IEC 7810 ID-1. Right, the embedded inlay: a copper antenna coil tuned to 13.56 MHz around the chip, which reads its UID over ISO/IEC 14443-A as an NFC Forum Type 2 tag; chip options NTAG213 (144 B), NTAG216 (888 B) and MIFARE Classic 1K (16 sectors).

bullets: Lamination stack: a printed front overlay (artwork, spot UV, metallic foil), a PVC core carrying the antenna coil and NFC chip module, and a printed back overlay for the fallback barcode and sequential card number.
One inlay, many chips: the same coil-and-chip construction takes NTAG213, NTAG216, MIFARE Classic 1K or MIFARE DESFire EV3 without changing the card body.

Finishing is the retention play: spot UV, metallic foil (gold, silver, holographic), soft-touch matte lamination, embossed numbering, die-cut shapes and transparent or frosted PVC earn wallet-slot residency over a paper punch card.
The barcode rides the print, not the chip: a 1D Code 128 or 2D QR carrying the same member-ID keeps the card working on lanes still waiting on NFC hardware.

sections.title: From tap to points — the POS flow in four moves
sections.intro: A loyalty tap is over before the customer has pocketed their payment card. The reader lifts the UID, the loyalty engine does the thinking, and the points post inside the same receipt — no app to open, no barcode to align. Weighing it against the sticker-and-scanner status quo? The [RFID vs barcode comparison](/compare/rfid-vs-barcode/) settles that half of the decision.

image.alt: Four-step tap-to-earn POS flow for an RFID loyalty card. Step 1, the customer taps the card on the POS NFC reader. Step 2, the reader captures the chip UID in < 100 ms at 13.56 MHz. Step 3, the loyalty engine (Yotpo, Smile.io or custom) maps the UID to the member record. Step 4, points, tier and promotions post and the receipt prints inside the normal transaction envelope. A phone-tap branch shows the same card opening a loyalty dashboard via an NDEF URL on an iPhone (iOS 12+) or Android phone, with no app install.

bullets: Tap: the customer taps the loyalty card on the NFC reader at the POS — no app to download, no card to hand over.

faq.question: How does the NFC loyalty card connect to our POS system?
faq.answer: Each NFC loyalty card has a unique chip ID (UID) that your POS system reads via an NFC reader connected to or integrated into the terminal. When the customer taps, the UID is sent to your loyalty software which looks up the customer record and applies the transaction. For simpler setups, the card can be programmed with an NDEF URL that opens a web-based loyalty page on the cashier's tablet when tapped. We work with your POS vendor or system integrator to ensure the card data format matches your system requirements.

faq.question: Can customers tap the loyalty card on their phone for self-service?
faq.answer: Yes. If the card is programmed with an NDEF URL record, any NFC-enabled smartphone (iPhone and Android) will open the URL when the card is tapped against the phone. This can link to the customer's loyalty balance page, a promotional offer or a registration form. This creates a hybrid physical+digital loyalty experience without requiring an app download.

faq.question: What is the MOQ and cost for custom loyalty cards?
faq.answer: MOQ is 500 for custom-printed NFC loyalty cards with NTAG213 chip. Pricing decreases significantly at 1,000, 2,500, 5,000 and 10,000+ quantities. Premium finishes (metallic foil, spot UV, embossing) add a small per-card premium. Contact us with your quantity, chip choice and finishing requirements for a detailed quotation.

faq.question: What is the production lead time, and can we get samples first?
faq.answer: Standard production runs 10-12 business days after artwork approval, with a 7-day rush available for promotional or seasonal launches. Free samples ship once artwork is locked, so you can approve card stock, print quality and chip encoding before committing the full run. Share your quantity, chip choice and finishing stack and we return a firm schedule.

faq.question: Which chip should we choose — NTAG213, NTAG216, MIFARE Classic 1K or MIFARE DESFire EV3?
faq.answer: NTAG213 (144 B) is the loyalty default: enough memory for a member-ID or a URL that opens the loyalty dashboard on phone-tap, at the lowest credible NFC cost. NTAG216 (888 B) suits programmes that want a welcome promo plus member-ID written into the NDEF payload on first tap. MIFARE Classic 1K gives 16 sectors for multi-merchant mall or plaza programmes that separate one merchant per sector. MIFARE DESFire EV3 adds AES-128 per-card key diversification where a stored-value or prepaid balance is stacked onto the loyalty card.

faq.question: Can you print our brand artwork and add per-card variable data?
faq.answer: Yes. Cards print full-colour by offset (MOQ 500) or UV digital (MOQ 100), with a premium finishing stack — spot UV, metallic foil, soft-touch lamination, embossed card numbers, die-cut shapes, and transparent or frosted PVC — that earns the card wallet-slot residency instead of the bin. Variable data is standard: sequential card numbers, a unique QR code per card, and a pre-programmed NDEF URL that opens each customer's loyalty dashboard when tapped on a phone.

faq.question: Can you pre-encode cards for our loyalty platform, and where does customer data live?
faq.answer: Yes. Proud Tek factory pre-encodes the chip UID and an optional NDEF URL, and ships a per-card manifest for import into your loyalty engine — Yotpo, Annex Cloud, Smile.io, Voucherify, Loyalty Lion, or a custom back-end. The card itself is only a UID carrier: the member record, points and tier live in the back-end, which keeps personal data off the card and lets GDPR access, erasure and portability requests be served from one system. If the card later carries a stored-value or payment-linked balance, PCI-DSS v4.0 scope applies to the back-end and POS path, not to the card.
